messages.subject: Same Chi-square and DF for different models
parts:
Hi,

I am running two models 
model 1: 


model 2:


The constructs and items are the same in both models. As you can see, model 2 is a modified version of model 1 where one of the IVs became the mediator. The parameter estimates and p values are coming as expected (I checked the results in AMOS as well). 

The problem is:  both the models are showing the same chi-square and DF. When I tried to compare the models using the ANOVA test, the results is 0, because of the same chi-square and DF. In AMOS every time I change something in a model (i.e., redesign the model with a mediator) it gives me a different set of chi-square and DF. Why lavaan is not giving me that? How can I test the model comparison?

I really appreciate it if someone can help. 


Regards,
Husain Akareem

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Same Chi-square and DF for different models
parts:
Husain,

To elaborate, the term you might search on for these is "equivalent models."

In your case, your model is saturated at the structural level in both versions. A saturated model just rearranges the terms to perfectly reproduce the variances and covariances--here, the variances and covariances you would get from the CFA. You haven't added or removed any restrictions on reproducing that VCV, so your df (which all arise from the measurement model) don't change.

Pat

You just changed some covariances between exogenous latent variables (model 1) to regression coefficients. Amos will give you the same result if you specify it as lavaan.

messages.author: 5abdb409f213d464
messages.subject: Re: Same Chi-square and DF for different models
parts:
Correct. You increase the number of regression coefficients, but at the same time you reduce the number of exogenous variables and the corresponding number of covariances. Pat has explained it in a technically versed way. You could possibly do the following:
(1) Model2 as unconstrained model
(2) Model3 with a == 0 and d == 0 as constrained model
Model3 is then *not* identical to Model1, but it might be roughly what you want to do? Maybe it's just a question of whether GRP acts as a mediator?

messages.subject: Re: Same Chi-square and DF for different models
parts:
Hi, I did not follow this so I ask in case others may not as well. A saturated model as I am used to the term is one in which there is a path from every variable to some other--no restrictions are imposed. Clearly model 1 has restrictions:
  1. mgt ⊥ sup
  2. mgt ⊥ grp
  3. sup ⊥ grp

and in model 2,  2.) and 3.) do not hold,, i.e. it puts more restrictions on the data. An equivalent model as I am used to the term are models that entail all the same dependencies/independencies in the data.  That is not true of these models. Maybe I am looking at this from the DAG causal model angle and I am definitely not clearing up Hussain's problem. Harold
On Fri, Dec 25, 2020 at 2:32 PM Patrick (Malone Quantitative) <mal...@malonequantitative.com> wrote:

Husain,

To elaborate, the term you might search on for these is "equivalent models."

In your case, your model is saturated at the structural level in both versions. A saturated model just rearranges the terms to perfectly reproduce the variances and covariances--here, the variances and covariances you would get from the CFA. You haven't added or removed any restrictions on reproducing that VCV, so your df (which all arise from the measurement model) don't change.

Pat

On Fri, Dec 25, 2020 at 6:03 AM <car...@web.de> wrote:
Apart from a few lines of code that are not really necessary (model 2) ... df = 554 for both models, correct? That's not very surprising. You just changed some covariances between exogenous latent variables (model 1) to regression coefficients. Amos will give you the same result if you specify it as lavaan.

Model 1:
model1 <- '
#constructs & items
mgt =~ mgt03 + mgt04 + mgt05 + mgt08 + mgt09 + mgt11 + mgt12
sup =~ sup02 + sup03 + sup04 + sup05 + sup06 + sup07 + sup08 + sup09 + sup10 + sup11 + sup12
grp =~ grp01 + grp02 + grp03 + grp04 + grp05 + grp06 + grp07 + grp08 + grp09 + grp10 + grp11
sb =~ sb01 + sb02 + sb03 + sb04 + sb05 + sb06

#regression
sb ~ mgt + sup + grp
'


Model 2:
model2 <- '
#constructs & items
mgt =~ mgt03 + mgt04 + mgt05 + mgt08 + mgt09 + mgt11 + mgt12
sup =~ sup02 + sup03 + sup04 + sup05 + sup06 + sup07 + sup08 + sup09 + sup10 + sup11 + sup12
grp =~ grp01 + grp02 + grp03 + grp04 + grp05 + grp06 + grp07 + grp08 + grp09 + grp10 + grp11
sb =~ sb01 + sb02 + sb03 + sb04 + sb05 + sb06

#estimtating the variances and covariances of the exogenous variables (mgt & sup)
mgt ~~ mgt
sup ~~ sup

mgt ~~ sup

#estimating the variances of residuals for endogenous variables (grp & sb)
grp ~~ grp
sb ~~ sb

#direct effects
grp ~ a*mgt+ d*sup
sb ~ c*mgt + e*sup + b*grp

#calculating specific indirect effect: mgt - grp - sb
SIE1 := a*b
#calculating specific indirect effect: sup - grp - sb
SIE2 := d*b

#calculating total effect of mgt & sup
TE_mgt := SIE1 + c
TE_sup := SIE2 + e
'
